source_text: Omnes autem dixit ad condemnationem per Adam et omnes ad iustificationem vitae per Iesum Christum, cum utique non omnes eos, qui moriuntur in Adam, transferat Christus ad vitam, sed omnes dixit atque omnes, quia sicut sine Adam nullus ad mortem, ita sine Christo nullus ad vitam. Sicut dicimus de litterarum magistro, si in civitate solus est: omnes iste hic litteras docet, non quia omnes discunt, sed quia nemo nisi ab ipso. Quos autem omnes dixerat, multos postea dixit, eosdem tamen omnes multosque significans. " Sicut enim per unius inoboedientiam peccatores constituti sunt multi, ita et per unius oboedientiam iusti constituentur multi " [n192] . Adhuc quaerat, per quid peccatum inveniatur in parvulo; respondent ei Paginae sanctae: " Per unum hominem peccatum in mundum intravit " [n193] . Sanctas quidem Apostoli esse paginas confitemur non ob aliud, nisi quia rationi pietati fidei congruentes erudiunt nos et Deum credere inviolabilis aequitatis et opera eius bona honestaque defendere et praeceptis eius moderationem prudentiam iustitiam vindicare.
pass_a_gloss: But he said all unto condemnation through Adam and all unto justification of life through Jesus Christ, when certainly Christ does not transfer all those who die in Adam unto life, but he said all and all, because as without Adam no one unto death, so without Christ no one unto life. As we say of a teacher of letters, if he is alone in a city: this man here teaches all letters, not because all learn, but because no one except from him. But those whom he had said all, he afterward said many, signifying nevertheless the same as all and many. 'For as through the disobedience of one many were constituted sinners, so also through the obedience of one many will be constituted just.' Let him still ask through what sin is found in a little child; the holy Pages answer him: 'Through one human being sin entered into the world.' We confess indeed that the Apostle's pages are holy not for another reason, except because, agreeing with reason, piety, faith, they instruct us both to believe God of inviolable equity and to defend his works as good and honorable and to vindicate moderation, prudence, justice for his precepts.

pass_b_english: You write: ‘He said “all” come through Adam to condemnation and “all” through Jesus Christ to justification of life. Certainly Christ does not transfer to life all those who die in Adam. He said “all” in both places because, just as no one comes to death without Adam, so no one comes to life without Christ. It is like what we say about a teacher of letters if he is the only one in a town: “This man teaches everyone here their letters.” Not everyone learns, but no one learns except from him. Those he had called “all” he afterward called “many,” yet signified the same people by “all” and “many”: “For just as through one man’s disobedience many were made sinners, so through one man’s obedience many will be made righteous” (Romans 5:19). Let him still ask through what sin is found in an infant. The holy pages answer him: “Through one man sin entered the world”’ (Romans 5:12; Augustine, Marriage and Desire 2.46–47). We indeed confess that the apostle’s pages are holy, for this reason alone: in agreement with reason, devotion, and faith, they teach us to believe in God’s inviolable justice, to defend his works as good and honorable, and to maintain the moderation, wisdom, and justice of his commands.
